answer: Because the meadow stake is held until the opal settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the anchor audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 23% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a inexpensive one. A farm running 145 keys thus forfeits that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation low-cost. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
